title: Ada and the Trail
premise: Beatrix Dravenmoor, a disgraced mountain guide hiding under a new name in the river town of Kessel's Landing, is dragged back into the trade when a supply expedition upriver goes silent and its desperate daughter, Ada, begs her to lead a rescue. With a crew of misfits—a defrocked cartographer, a mute boatman, and Ada herself—Beatrix follows the Veyl River toward its forbidden source, where she once lost her own expedition and earned her blacklist. As monsoon clouds gather and sabotage reveals someone aboard knows what really happened at the source years ago, Beatrix must choose between protecting her invented life and telling the truth that will either save them or destroy them all. In the end, she confesses her role in the old disaster at the source itself, trading her last shred of anonymity for Ada's survival, and the found family they've built carries them home through the flood—not forgiven by the world, but no longer running from it.
about_author: Sable Thackeray is a former river outfitter who spent a decade leading expeditions through remote mountain watersheds before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for unsentimental wilderness prose and characters who earn their redemption the hard way.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Her Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix, living quietly as a ferry mechanic in Kessel's Landing, watches a supply expedition depart upriver and recognizes the route—the one that ruined her. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: uneasy foreboding beneath a carefully constructed calm.

chapters.title: Ada at the Dock
chapters.summary: Ada Vance, seventeen, arrives searching for anyone willing to go after her father's silent expedition; the town's guides refuse. She finds Beatrix by tracing an old tattoo to a name that shouldn't exist. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: stubborn hope colliding with a stranger's cold refusal.

chapters.title: Blacklist
chapters.summary: Beatrix refuses, but a customs officer recognizes her and threatens exposure unless she leaves town—forcing her hand. She agrees to guide Ada upstream as far as the last radio relay, nothing more. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: They assemble a crew: Odell, a cartographer struck off the guild rolls; Tam, a boatman who hasn't spoken since a wreck he won't explain; and Juno, a cook with smuggler's maps. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: fragile camaraderie forming among people with something to hide.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: The run through the Serrated Narrows nearly capsizes them; Beatrix's skill saves the boat but Ada sees the terror beneath her competence. At night, the first relay station is found burned. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to dread—the silence isn't accidental.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Salvage from the missing expedition surfaces: a crushed crate stamped with Beatrix's old company mark, which she buried years ago. Someone has been here before them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: suspicion of her guide begins to take root.

chapters.title: Odell's Map
chapters.summary: Odell reveals the source valley was erased from official charts by decree—and that his own disgrace came from mapping it anyway. He shows Beatrix a hidden survey line only she could confirm. POV: Odell. Emotional beat: two exiles recognizing each other's scars.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: A grueling overland portage around the falls tests the crew; Tam finally speaks, one word, guiding Beatrix's rope work through whiteout spray. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: trust built through shared labor rather than words.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Their fuel cache is found contaminated; someone among them or shadowing them wants the journey stopped. Beatrix quietly investigates each crew member. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a winch.

chapters.title: Ada's Evidence
chapters.summary: Ada confronts Beatrix with letters proving Beatrix led the doomed expedition seven years ago—the one that killed Ada's uncle. The truth of their connection detonates between them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: betrayal, grief, and the question of whether to turn back.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Weather signals confirm the monsoon will make landfall in nine days; retreat would take eleven. They vote to push on. Beatrix, hollowed out, leads them into the gorge country. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: guilt converted into grim resolve.

chapters.title: The Watcher on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Juno spots a figure tracking them along the high ground—dressed in expedition gear a decade out of date. That night, their spare rope is cut. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: the wilderness stops being the most dangerous thing out here.

chapters.title: Gorge Country
chapters.summary: A rockslide traps the boat; Tam dives into flood-swollen water to free it and nearly drowns, saved by Ada. The crew bonds hardens into something like family. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: loyalty forged in near-loss.

chapters.title: Camp of the Lost Expedition
chapters.summary: They find the frozen-in-time campsite of Beatrix's old team—tents, journals, and evidence contradicting the official story of what happened at the source. Beatrix reads her own seven-year-old handwriting. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: confronting the ghost she became.

chapters.title: The Journal's Lie
chapters.summary: Ada discovers pages torn from the journal—pages that would clear Beatrix or condemn her further. Odell admits he tore them out years ago and has been carrying them ever since. POV: Odell. Emotional beat: the cost of protecting a friend from the truth.

chapters.title: The Watcher Comes Down
chapters.summary: The stalker reveals himself: Merrick, the expedition's supposed-dead radio operator, who survived the old disaster and has been sabotaging anyone approaching the source to keep its secret buried. POV: Merrick. Emotional beat: a villain shaped by the same wound as the heroes.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Weir
chapters.summary: Merrick takes Ada hostage at the final weir, demanding they all turn back; Beatrix offers him the torn journal pages in exchange. A tense negotiation cracks open what really happened at the source. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: bargaining with her own past.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the forbidden headwaters: a glacial cathedral where the old disaster's cause is revealed—an unreported dam collapse, covered up by the company that blacklisted Beatrix to bury its liability. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: awe and fury intertwined.

chapters.title: Confession at the Headwaters
chapters.summary: Beatrix publicly confesses her one true failure—that she ordered the crossing that put her team in the collapse zone—surrendering her anonymity so the record can finally be corrected. Merrick, given the truth he wanted, stands down. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits early; the descent becomes a race against rising water. Merrick, redeemed by purpose, uses his knowledge of the old routes to lead them through channels only he remembers. POV: Merrick. Emotional beat: an enemy becoming crew.

chapters.title: Through the Flood
chapters.summary: The climactic run down the flooded gorge: the boat is destroyed, and they survive by lashing together salvaged gear, each member's skill indispensable. They reach Kessel's Landing battered, half-drowned, alive. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: unity in the teeth of annihilation.

chapters.title: The Names We Keep
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the dam-collapse testimony reaches the capital; Beatrix's name is cleared though her old life is gone forever. Ada stays on as her apprentice, and the crew refits the boat for a new season. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—found family, chosen truth, a future on the water.
